column3: MT 22:1–2; the following verses of this psalm are MT +1. Close to the Hebrew; the tune name is translated “Set to ‘The Deer of the Dawn,’” NKJV capitalizes “Me… My” as messianic, and “my deliverance” is rendered “helping Me.”
Close to the Hebrew; “there is no repose for me” is rendered “and am not silent.”
Close to the Hebrew; יוֹשֵׁב (“sitting, enthroned”) is rendered “Enthroned.”
Close to the Hebrew; “they open wide with the lip” is rendered “They shoot out the lip,” and NKJV supplies “saying.”
Close to the Hebrew; the imperative גֹּל (“commit, roll”) is rendered as narrative, “He trusted in the LORD.”
Close to the Hebrew; כַּחֶרֶשׂ (“like earthenware”) is rendered “like a potsherd.”
The Masoretic text reads כָּאֲרִי (“like a lion [at] my hands and feet”); NKJV renders “They pierced My hands and My feet,” following the Septuagint and some manuscripts.
Close to the Hebrew; יְחִידָתִי (“my only one”) is rendered “My precious life,” and “hand” “power.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV capitalizes “from Him… He cried,” referring to the sufferer as messianic.
Close to the Hebrew; עֲנָוִים (“the humble”) is rendered “The poor.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the fat ones of the earth” is rendered “the prosperous,” and the last line “Even he who cannot keep himself alive.”
Close to the Hebrew; “to the generation” is rendered “to the next generation.”
